Name: T's Core
Author: tikamin557
Description:
[color=#ffff00][size=6][b]About T's Core[/b][/size][/color]
T's Core is a shared library and framework for Stardew Valley mods.
It provides reusable systems and additional features for both SMAPI mods and Content Patcher Content Packs.

[b][size=4][color=#00ff00]For players[/color]:[/size][/b]
T's Core does not add standalone gameplay content by itself. In most cases, you only need to install it when another mod lists T's Core as a requirement.

[b][size=4][color=#00ff00]For mod authors[/color]:[/size][/b]
T's Core provides additional systems that can be used to create features which would otherwise require custom C# code, as well as shared APIs and development tools for more advanced mods.
Many features can be used directly from a Content Patcher Content Pack without writing any C# code.
[line]
[color=#ffff00][size=6][b]Documentation[/b][/size][/color]
Detailed documentation, JSON formats, examples, API references, and Content Pack guides are available on GitHub:
[u][url=https://github.com/Tikamin557/Ts-Core/tree/main/docs][size=5]GitHub Documentation[/size][/url][/u]
The GitHub documentation is actively maintained and expanded with new guides, examples, and API documentation as T's Core evolves.
[line]
[color=#00ffff][b][size=6]What Can T's Core Do?[/size][/b][/color]
Some of the main features available to mod authors are described below.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Content Patcher Integration[/b][/size][/color]
T's Core provides additional features specifically for Content Patcher Content Packs.

[b][color=#00ff00]Conditional GMCM options[/color][/b]
Additional ConfigSchema properties can control whether a setting is displayed in Generic Mod Config Menu depending on which mods are installed.
[code]TsCore.ShowIfMod[/code]Shows the setting if at least one of the specified mods is installed.
[code]TsCore.ShowIfAllMods[/code]Shows the setting only if all specified mods are installed.
Both properties support multiple comma-separated mod IDs and can be used together.
This can be useful for compatibility settings which should only appear when the corresponding mod is installed.

[b][color=#00ff00]Content Pack development and reloading[/color][/b]
The developer command:
[code]tscore_cp_reload <ContentPackId>[/code]can reload many Content Patcher Content Pack changes while Stardew Valley is still running.
It can refresh:
[list]
[*][code]content.json[/code]and patches[/*]
[*][code]ConfigSchema[/code][/*]
[*][code]config.json[/code][/*]
[*]Config Tokens[/*]
[*]GMCM settings[/*]
[*]Dynamic Tokens[/*]
[*]Dynamic Token conditions and dependencies[/*]
[/list]This can significantly reduce the number of game restarts needed while developing and testing Content Patcher mods.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]T's Core Content Packs[/b][/size][/color]
Many T's Core features can be added through Content Packs without writing C# code.
T's Core Content Packs can currently register:
[list]
[*]Building Providers[/*]
[*]Warp Providers[/*]
[*]Notification Themes[/*]
[*]Migration definitions[/*]
[/list]This makes these systems available to Content Patcher mod authors as well as C# mod authors.
Detailed setup instructions and JSON examples for each system are available in the GitHub Modder Guide.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Warp Actions & Warp Providers[/b][/size][/color]
Add custom warps and teleportation effects, including configurable visual effects, sounds, timing, and screen transitions.
Warp Providers can also determine destinations dynamically at runtime instead of requiring fixed coordinates.
This is useful for mods which need to warp the player to locations that may move or change depending on other installed mods.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Building Providers[/b][/size][/color]
Add additional functionality to custom buildings.
Building Providers can provide features such as:
[list]
[*]Night-time lights[/*]
[*]Additional conditional draw layers[/*]
[*]Animated building layers[/*]
[*]Enable/disable controls for individual building features[/*]
[*]Restrictions on where buildings can be constructed[/*]
[/list]These features can be defined through a T's Core Content Pack without writing C# code.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Notification System[/b][/size][/color]
Display customizable HUD notifications from your mod.
Notification Themes can control the appearance and behavior of notifications, and can be reused by multiple notifications.
Notifications can also be triggered through Trigger Actions.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Migration System[/b][/size][/color]
Safely migrate IDs stored in existing save data when a mod changes an ID in a future update.
For example, if the internal ID of a custom building needs to be changed, T's Core can migrate existing placed buildings from the old ID to the new ID when the save is loaded.
This helps mod authors make internal changes without requiring players to manually remove and rebuild affected content.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Content Patcher Tokens[/b][/size][/color]
T's Core provides reusable Content Patcher tokens which other Content Packs can use.
These include information provided by T's Core systems, such as relationship and location-related data.
See the GitHub documentation for the currently available tokens.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Relationship & Location Services[/b][/size][/color]
T's Core provides shared relationship and location information which can be used by other mods.
Relationship Services provide unified partner information and support multiple relationship systems.
Current relationship integrations include:
[list]
[*]Vanilla relationships[/*]
[*]PolyamorySweetLove[/*]
[*]FreeLove[/*]
[/list]Location Services provide reusable player and location-related information for other T's Core features and integrations.

[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Shared APIs[/b][/size][/color]
SMAPI C# mods can access T's Core systems through public APIs.
This allows multiple mods to share common functionality instead of implementing the same systems independently.
Public APIs and examples are documented in the GitHub Modder Guide.
[line]
[color=#ffff00][size=6][b]Installation[/b][/size][/color]
Install T's Core using your preferred mod manager, or extract the downloaded archive into your Stardew Valley "[color=#fce5cd]Mods[/color]" folder.
T's Core requires SMAPI and Content Patcher.
If another mod requires T's Core, simply install it along with the required dependencies before launching the game.
[line]
[color=#ffff00][size=6][b]For C# Mod Developers[/b][/size][/color]
T's Core also provides public services and APIs for SMAPI C# mods.
Current systems include:
[list]
[*]Relationship Services[/*]
[*]Location Services[/*]
[*]Warp Services[/*]
[*]Building Services[/*]
[*]Migration Services[/*]
[*]Notification Services[/*]
[*]Content Patcher integration[/*]
[*]Shared utilities[/*]
[/list]Only documented public APIs should be used by other mods. Internal implementations may change between versions.
See the GitHub Modder Guide for API documentation and usage examples.
[line]
[color=#ffff00][size=6][b]Compatibility[/b][/size][/color]
T's Core is designed to provide reusable systems that can be shared between mods and to improve compatibility where runtime information is needed.
For example, Warp Providers can resolve destinations at runtime instead of relying entirely on fixed map coordinates. This can make warp-based mods more adaptable to custom maps or other mods which change locations and destinations.
Relationship Services also provide a unified interface for supported relationship systems.
Additional integrations and systems may be added in future versions.
[line]
[color=#ffff00][size=6][b]API Stability[/b][/size][/color]
T's Core is under active development.
Public APIs are intended to remain compatible whenever possible, but new functionality and optional Content Pack properties may be added as T's Core continues to develop.
When developing against T's Core:
[list]
[*]Use documented public APIs whenever possible.[/*]
[*]Avoid relying on internal implementation details.[/*]
[*]Keep your required T's Core version up to date.[/*]
[*]Test your mod after updating T's Core.[/*]
[/list][line]
